question: Non-communicable diseases are best described as diseases which:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. are not transmitted from person to person and are usually of long duration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, cancer and chronic lung disease are not transmitted from person to person and usually last for years

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — occur only in children: They occur mainly in adults and their burden rises with age

C — last for less than a week: A short duration is the feature of acute infections

D — spread from one person to another through contact: Person to person spread is the character of communicable diseases

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because they last for life, the aim of care is to prevent complications and to keep the patient functioning, rather than to cure
option_1: are not transmitted from person to person and are usually of long duration
option_4: spread from one person to another through contact

question: Under the national programme for non-communicable diseases, population based screening is offered to all persons above the age of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 30 years

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Every person of thirty years and above is screened for high blood pressure, high blood sugar and the common cancers at the health and wellness centres

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 18 years: Screening from eighteen years is not the programme norm, though younger persons with risk factors are also assessed

C — 45 years: Screening does not wait until forty five years

D — 60 years: Starting at sixty years would miss the great majority of those at risk

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The screening is linked to treatment and follow-up, since detecting a raised blood sugar is of no value unless the person is treated and reviewed

question: In health education the letters IEC stand for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Information, Education and Communication

🧠 Clinical Rationale: IEC stands for Information, Education and Communication, the activities through which people are given knowledge and helped to change behaviour

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Immunisation, Eradication and Control: These words belong to disease control programmes

B — Infection, Examination and Cure: These words describe clinical activities and not the concept of IEC

D — Investigation, Evaluation and Correction: These words are used in an audit and not in health education

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Information alone rarely changes behaviour, which is why education and communication with the community are added to it

question: The most suitable method of health education for a group of illiterate village women is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a group discussion with the help of pictures and a flannelgraph

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pictures with spoken discussion overcome illiteracy and allow questions, which is why they are the method of choice for such a group

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a printed pamphlet: A pamphlet is useless to a person who cannot read

B — a circular sent to the house: A circular reaches the house but not the understanding of the person

D — a lecture in English: A lecture in English does not communicate with the audience

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Local words and locally drawn pictures are prepared in advance, since a picture that the audience cannot recognise teaches nothing
option_3: a group discussion with the help of pictures and a flannelgraph

question: A 55-year-old man attending a screening camp has a body mass index of 31, a blood pressure of 150/95 mm Hg and a fasting blood glucose of 130 milligrams per decilitre. This combination of findings is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. metabolic syndrome

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Central obesity with raised blood pressure and raised fasting glucose is the cluster known as metabolic syndrome, which greatly raises the risk of heart attack and stroke

🔍 Key Clues: 55-year-old | 95 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — malabsorption syndrome: Malabsorption presents with diarrhoea and weight loss

B — nephrotic syndrome: Nephrotic syndrome presents with protein in the urine and generalised oedema

C — wasting syndrome: Wasting syndrome is associated with severe malnutrition or advanced disease

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A person with this cluster needs combined management of weight, blood pressure, sugar and lipids rather than treatment of one number alone

question: A 48-year-old man who has chewed tobacco for twenty years has a white patch on the buccal mucosa that cannot be wiped off. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. advise him to stop tobacco at once and refer him for examination and biopsy if required

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A non removable white patch may be a pre-malignant lesion, so the habit must stop and the lesion must be examined and biopsied

🔍 Key Clues: 48-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — reassure him that it will disappear by itself: Reassurance without examination delays the diagnosis of a cancer that is curable when found early

C — apply an antiseptic ointment and review after six months: An ointment does not treat a pre-malignant lesion and a six month delay is too long

D — give him an antibiotic: Antibiotics have no role in a white patch

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: At the same visit he is shown the lesion in a mirror and helped to fix a date to quit, since advice given at the moment of discovery is most effective
option_1: reassure him that it will disappear by itself
option_2: advise him to stop tobacco at once and refer him for examination and biopsy if required
option_3: apply an antiseptic ointment and review after six months

question: A 50-year-old woman has a painless, hard lump in the right breast that is fixed to the underlying tissue. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. refer her at once for clinical examination and further investigation such as mammography and biopsy

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A painless, hard and fixed lump is suspicious of cancer and needs prompt assessment and biopsy

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — prescribe an antibiotic: An antibiotic has no effect on a solid lump

B — tell her to come back if the lump becomes painful: Waiting for pain wastes valuable time, as early breast cancer is usually painless

C — advise her to apply a warm compress for a month: A warm compress is useless and delays the diagnosis

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also teaches breast self examination to all women above twenty and records that it has been demonstrated
option_2: tell her to come back if the lump becomes painful
option_3: advise her to apply a warm compress for a month
option_4: refer her at once for clinical examination and further investigation such as mammography and biopsy

question: A 45-year-old woman has a blood stained vaginal discharge and has never been screened for cancer of the cervix. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. refer her for a speculum examination with a cervical smear or visual inspection with acetic acid as per the programme

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A blood stained discharge in a woman above thirty needs a cervical examination and screening or biopsy without delay

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her a vaginal pessary: A pessary treats a local infection and not a suspected growth

C — advise her to wait until she reaches menopause: Waiting until menopause loses years during which a pre-cancerous lesion is easily treated

D — treat her with a course of antibiotics and review later: An antibiotic without examining the cervix may allow a cancer to progress

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Screening is repeated as per the programme, because a single normal report does not give lifelong protection
option_2: refer her for a speculum examination with a cervical smear or visual inspection with acetic acid as per the programme
option_3: advise her to wait until she reaches menopause
option_4: treat her with a course of antibiotics and review later

question: A 52-year-old man is found to have a blood pressure of 170/110 mm Hg with headache at a screening camp. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. let him rest for five minutes, repeat the measurement, refer him to the medical officer at once and advise salt restriction and follow-up

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Such a high reading with headache needs confirmation after rest and urgent medical review, along with immediate lifestyle advice and a plan for follow-up

🔍 Key Clues: 52-year-old | 110 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell him that a single high reading is of no importance: A single severe reading must never be dismissed without assessment

B — advise him to take a painkiller and go home: A painkiller does not lower the blood pressure and the cause remains

C — record the reading and ask him to come after a month: A month's delay risks a stroke or heart attack

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: If the headache is associated with vomiting or blurred vision, the possibility of a hypertensive emergency makes emergency referral urgent
option_1: tell him that a single high reading is of no importance
option_2: advise him to take a painkiller and go home
option_3: record the reading and ask him to come after a month
option_4: let him rest for five minutes, repeat the measurement, refer him to the medical officer at once and advise salt restriction and follow-up

question: A 58-year-old man with known diabetes has a fasting blood glucose of 250 milligrams per decilitre but no symptoms. Under the NCD programme the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. repeat the test for confirmation, refer him for treatment and arrange regular follow-up and checks of his eyes, feet and kidneys

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A high reading is repeated for confirmation and the patient is treated and followed up with periodic examination of the eyes, feet, kidneys and blood pressure

🔍 Key Clues: 58-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — say that nothing needs to be done as he feels well: Symptoms are a poor guide, as complications begin long before they appear

C — tell him to come back only if his sugar crosses 400: Waiting for a very high value invites complications in the meantime

D — advise him to stop taking his medicine: Stopping the medicine would make the control worse

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the weight, blood pressure and foot examination at every visit, as complications are prevented rather than treated
option_1: repeat the test for confirmation, refer him for treatment and arrange regular follow-up and checks of his eyes, feet and kidneys
option_2: say that nothing needs to be done as he feels well
option_3: tell him to come back only if his sugar crosses 400
option_4: advise him to stop taking his medicine

question: The annual estimates of the birth rate, the death rate and the infant mortality rate for the whole country are provided by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Sample Registration System

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Sample Registration System collects data continuously from a representative sample of villages and urban blocks and brings out the annual rates for the state and the country

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Civil Registration System: The Civil Registration System records individual births and deaths but does not by itself provide reliable national rates

B — National Family Health Survey: The family health survey is carried out at intervals of several years

D — decennial census: The census is held once in ten years and does not give annual rates

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: These official rates are what the nurse quotes when her own district is compared with the state, so it is worth remembering that they are estimates from a sample and not exact counts

question: Which single figure is generally used as the most sensitive index of the health status of a community?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the infant mortality rate

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The infant mortality rate reflects maternal health, delivery care, nutrition, immunisation and the standard of living, so it responds quickly to any change in the health services

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the crude death rate: The crude death rate is influenced by the age structure of the population

B — the growth rate of the population: The growth rate is a composite of births, deaths and migration

D — the birth rate: The birth rate mainly reflects fertility

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The neonatal part of the rate points to the quality of delivery and newborn care, and the post neonatal part to the home environment

question: In a village, out of 200 children born alive in a year, 10 died before completing one year of age. The infant mortality rate per 1000 live births is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 50

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Ten deaths among two hundred live births gives fifty deaths per thousand live births

🔍 Key Clues: infant

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20: Twenty would mean four deaths, which is not the case

B — 5: Five would mean one death

C — 10: Ten is the raw number of deaths and not a rate

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The district figure is compared with the state and national rates so that the community's own performance can be judged

question: A village recorded 8 deaths during a year and had a mid-year population of 4000. The crude death rate per 1000 population is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 2

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Eight deaths in a population of four thousand gives two deaths per thousand in the year

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 32: Thirty two would need sixty four deaths

C — 0.2: Point two would mean less than one death, which is incorrect

D — 8: Eight is the number of deaths and not the rate

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The death rate is itself a crude measure, and it is broken down by age and by cause to make it useful for planning

question: Which of the following is an example of a mass media method of health education?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a radio talk on prevention of dengue

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Radio, television, newspapers and posters reach large numbers of people at the same time and are therefore called mass media

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a consultation between the nurse and one patient: A consultation reaches one person only

C — a one to one counselling session at the clinic: Counselling at the clinic is interpersonal and not mass communication

D — a group discussion in a home: A discussion in a home reaches one family

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Mass media create awareness, while personal methods change behaviour, so the two are used together
option_1: a radio talk on prevention of dengue
option_2: a consultation between the nurse and one patient
option_3: a one to one counselling session at the clinic

question: The main advantage of interpersonal communication over mass media in health education is that it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. allows two way communication with immediate feedback and clarification of doubts

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Face to face discussion allows questions, correction of wrong beliefs and attention to the individual's own situation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — reaches a very large number of people at once: Large reach is the strength of mass media and not of personal communication

B — costs the least per person reached: Mass media cost less per person reached

D — needs no skill on the part of the health worker: Interpersonal methods demand even more skill and preparation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: This is why a mother who has been personally shown how to prepare oral rehydration solution uses it correctly, while one who has only heard a radio talk often does not
option_1: reaches a very large number of people at once
option_3: allows two way communication with immediate feedback and clarification of doubts
option_4: needs no skill on the part of the health worker

question: A flannelgraph is widely used in rural health education because it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. holds cut out pictures that can be added or removed to build a story before the eyes of the audience

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The flannel board holds the pictures by friction, so the story can be built step by step exactly as the talk proceeds

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — needs no preparation at all: Good pictures and their order must be prepared in advance

C — works without the presence of a health worker: It requires a trained person to present the story and answer questions

D — can be read aloud to a large audience: It is a visual aid and not a text to be read out

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Using the audience's own locality in the pictures makes the message far more convincing than a printed illustration
option_2: holds cut out pictures that can be added or removed to build a story before the eyes of the audience
option_3: works without the presence of a health worker
option_4: can be read aloud to a large audience

question: Toilets were built in a village under a government scheme last year, but the nurse finds that most families still defecate in the open and use the toilets only to store grain. The most effective action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. find out the reasons from the families, involve the village leaders and women's groups, hold discussions at the site and follow up with practical solutions to their objections

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Behaviour change follows understanding and ownership, so the real reasons must be discovered and answered with the community's own leaders taking part

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — get more toilets built: Building more toilets that are not used adds no health benefit

C — ask the health staff to visit every morning and stop the practice: Policing by the staff does not last a day after the visits stop

D — report the families to the district authorities: Reporting to the authorities punishes the families without solving the problem

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Common real reasons are the lack of water, the fear of the pit filling up and the habit of going in groups, and each has a practical answer
option_2: find out the reasons from the families, involve the village leaders and women's groups, hold discussions at the site and follow up with practical solutions to their objections
option_3: ask the health staff to visit every morning and stop the practice
option_4: report the families to the district authorities

question: A population based approach to the prevention of non-communicable diseases means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. applying measures such as tobacco control, reduction of salt and sugar in food, health promotion and physical activity to the whole community

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A population approach tries to shift the risk of the whole community a little, which prevents many more cases than treating a few high risk persons

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — giving medicines to everyone above forty: Medicine for everyone is neither safe nor affordable

C — treating only those who come to the hospital: Waiting for patients to come is a clinical and not a population approach

D — screening only persons with a family history: Screening only those with a family history misses most cases

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse works on both fronts, promoting healthy habits in the whole village and finding and treating the individuals at high risk
option_2: applying measures such as tobacco control, reduction of salt and sugar in food, health promotion and physical activity to the whole community
option_3: treating only those who come to the hospital
option_4: screening only persons with a family history

question: A 40-year-old man whose father died of a heart attack asks how he can prevent the same illness. The nurse should advise him to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. stop tobacco and alcohol, keep his weight and blood pressure normal, take at least thirty minutes of exercise a day and get a periodic check of blood sugar and lipids

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A family history cannot be changed, but tobacco, weight, blood pressure, blood sugar, lipids and inactivity can all be modified, and together they remove most of the risk

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — get himself tested only when symptoms appear: Waiting for symptoms misses the long silent period during which prevention still works

C — take a vitamin tablet daily: A vitamin tablet does not protect the heart

D — avoid all fat in the diet for the rest of his life: Removing all fat is neither necessary nor sustainable, and the type of fat matters more than the quantity

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The advice is written down as specific goals, since a list of changes given verbally is rarely followed
option_1: stop tobacco and alcohol, keep his weight and blood pressure normal, take at least thirty minutes of exercise a day and get a periodic check of blood sugar and lipids
option_2: get himself tested only when symptoms appear
option_4: avoid all fat in the diet for the rest of his life

question: During a heat wave the nurse finds a 70-year-old man with hot dry skin, no sweating and confusion after working in the sun. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. move him to a cool shaded place, remove excess clothing, cool him actively with wet cloths or water, give fluids if he is conscious, and arrange urgent transfer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are the signs of heat stroke, in which the body's cooling has failed, and immediate active cooling along with transfer is life saving

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give him a strong painkiller and let him rest in the sun: A painkiller does not treat heat stroke and exposure continues

B — ask him to walk to the nearest hospital: Making him walk increases heat production and is dangerous

D — give him a hot drink and cover him with a blanket: Warmth and covering raise the body temperature further

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The very old, the very young and those working out of doors are the groups most affected, and the nurse teaches families to keep water and shade ready in advance
option_1: give him a strong painkiller and let him rest in the sun
option_2: ask him to walk to the nearest hospital
option_3: move him to a cool shaded place, remove excess clothing, cool him actively with wet cloths or water, give fluids if he is conscious, and arrange urgent transfer
option_4: give him a hot drink and cover him with a blanket

question: A 65-year-old woman is bedridden at home after a fracture of the neck of the femur. The most important nursing measure to prevent complications is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. change her position at least every two hours, keep the skin clean and dry, encourage deep breathing, adequate fluids and a protein rich diet

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Turning, skin care, breathing exercises, fluids and good nutrition together prevent pressure sores, chest infection, constipation and dehydration

🔍 Key Clues: 65-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep her flat on her back without any movement: Keeping her still in one position causes pressure sores and chest infection within days

B — restrict her fluids to reduce the need for a bedpan: Restricting fluids causes dehydration, concentrated urine and infection

D — massage the bony prominences vigorously every day: Vigorous massage over a bony prominence damages the tissue that is already under pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The family is taught to do these measures themselves, since a bedridden patient at home depends entirely on them
option_1: keep her flat on her back without any movement
option_2: restrict her fluids to reduce the need for a bedpan
option_3: change her position at least every two hours, keep the skin clean and dry, encourage deep breathing, adequate fluids and a protein rich diet
option_4: massage the bony prominences vigorously every day

question: Four cases of snake bite occur in a village during the harvest season. The nurse should advise the community and the families to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. keep the patient calm and still with the bitten limb immobilised at or below the level of the heart, avoid traditional remedies, and arrange the fastest possible transport to a facility with antivenom

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Immobilising the limb and keeping the patient calm slows the spread of venom, and the only definite treatment is antivenom given as early as possible

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give the patient a strong drink of alcohol for the pain: Alcohol increases the blood flow and worsens the poisoning

B — wait at home and observe whether swelling develops: Waiting at home allows the venom to act before treatment begins

D — apply a tight tourniquet above the bite and cut the wound: A tight tourniquet causes gangrene and cutting the wound increases bleeding and infection

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The species of the snake is not needed to start treatment, and the patient is never made to walk to the road
option_1: give the patient a strong drink of alcohol for the pain
option_2: wait at home and observe whether swelling develops
option_3: keep the patient calm and still with the bitten limb immobilised at or below the level of the heart, avoid traditional remedies, and arrange the fastest possible transport to a facility with antivenom
option_4: apply a tight tourniquet above the bite and cut the wound

question: A child in a village has drunk pesticide that was stored in a soft drink bottle and is now drowsy with frothy secretions in the mouth. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. clear the airway, turn the child to the side, give nothing by mouth and arrange immediate transfer to hospital with the container

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The airway is secured first, and vomiting is never induced because the vomit may be inhaled; the container identifies the poison and guides the treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — wait to see whether symptoms develop: Waiting allows absorption to continue, often leading to respiratory failure

C — give the child milk to drink: Milk is not an antidote and delays transfer

D — make the child vomit by giving salt water: Salt water induces vomiting and risks aspiration and salt poisoning

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also advises the community to keep pesticides in their original labelled containers, locked away from children
option_1: clear the airway, turn the child to the side, give nothing by mouth and arrange immediate transfer to hospital with the container
option_4: make the child vomit by giving salt water

question: Secondary prevention of disease means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. early detection of disease and prompt treatment to stop its progress

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Secondary prevention works at the stage when the disease has begun but is still early, as in screening and early treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the control of risk factors in the whole community: Control of risk factors in the whole population is also primary prevention

C — rehabilitation of a person with a disability: Rehabilitation is tertiary prevention

D — health promotion before any disease occurs: Measures before disease begins are primary prevention

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Screening programmes for hypertension, diabetes and cancer are examples of secondary prevention and depend mainly on nurses
option_1: early detection of disease and prompt treatment to stop its progress
option_2: the control of risk factors in the whole community
option_3: rehabilitation of a person with a disability

question: Which of the following is a primary prevention measure for cancer of the cervix?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. human papillomavirus vaccination along with health education on personal hygiene and the avoidance of tobacco

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vaccination and the control of risk factors act before the disease begins and are therefore primary prevention

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — treatment of an early cancer: Treatment of an established cancer is tertiary prevention

C — a cervical smear every three years: A smear detects a lesion that has already begun, so it is secondary prevention

D — biopsy of a suspicious lesion: A biopsy is a diagnostic step

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The vaccine is given in early adolescence, before exposure to the virus, which is why the school health service plays an important part
option_1: human papillomavirus vaccination along with health education on personal hygiene and the avoidance of tobacco

question: Three children under two years of age in a village develop fever with a rash within a week and none of them had been immunised against measles. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. report the outbreak at once, isolate the children at home during the infectious period, give the prescribed vitamin A, immunise the unimmunised children of the area and search for further cases

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An outbreak of measles is responded to by notification, isolation of the infectious cases, vitamin A for the patients, vaccination of the susceptible children and a search for more cases

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — close the anganwadi centre permanently: Closing the centre permanently harms the nutrition and vaccination of all the children

B — send the children to the district hospital without taking any other step: Referral alone leaves the outbreak uncontrolled in the village

C — start all the village children on antibiotics: Measles is viral, so antibiotics do not treat it

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because measles spreads by air, the susceptible children in the same and neighbouring lanes are immunised immediately, along with a check of the cold chain
option_2: send the children to the district hospital without taking any other step
option_3: start all the village children on antibiotics
option_4: report the outbreak at once, isolate the children at home during the infectious period, give the prescribed vitamin A, immunise the unimmunised children of the area and search for further cases

question: Which of the following is an example of a primary group in society?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the family

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A primary group is small, face to face and bound by close personal ties, of which the family and the play group are the classic examples

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a political party: A political party is a secondary group with an organised purpose

B — a cooperative bank: A cooperative bank is a formal institution

C — a trade union: A trade union is a large formal organisation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The primary group is where health habits, food practices and attitudes to treatment are first formed, which is why the nurse works through the family

question: Social change in a community is brought about mainly by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. education, urbanisation, new technology, legislation and the movement of people

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Change comes from new knowledge, migration to cities, technology, laws and contact with other ways of living, all of which interact with one another

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the weather and the seasons: Climate affects daily life but does not by itself change social institutions

B — the number of health centres in the area: Health centres influence health behaviour and not the whole structure of society

D — the size of the population alone: The size of the population is one factor among many

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

question: The main purpose of randomisation in an experimental study is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. make the groups comparable by distributing known and unknown factors equally between them

question: A patient with cirrhosis of the liver and ascites should be advised a diet that is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. low in salt but with adequate protein, energy and vitamins, taken in small frequent meals

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Salt restriction reduces the accumulation of fluid, while adequate protein and energy prevent muscle wasting, and small frequent meals are better tolerated

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — very low in protein and high in salt: Severe protein restriction causes malnutrition and is harmful unless there is frank encephalopathy

question: A 60-year-old man with heart failure has ankle swelling and has gained 3 kilograms in a week. The nurse should advise him to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. restrict salt in the diet, weigh himself daily on the same scale, take the prescribed diuretic regularly and report a gain of more than one kilogram in a day

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Salt restriction, a daily weight record and regular diuretic treatment prevent the fluid build-up, and a rapid gain is the earliest sign of decompensation

question: A 55-year-old man with a colostomy complains of excessive gas and odour from the bag. The nurse should advise him to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. avoid gas forming foods such as beans, cabbage and onions, eat slowly with the mouth closed, avoid very hot and very cold drinks, and use an odour proof bag that is changed regularly

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gas is produced by swallowed air and by certain foods, and both the eating habits and the food choices can be adjusted

A — eat very quickly so that the meal is over soon: Eating quickly increases the amount of air swallowed and produces more gas

question: A 70-year-old bedridden patient has a pressure ulcer over the sacrum. The dietary advice should be a diet:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. high in protein and calories with vitamin C, zinc and adequate fluids, in small frequent feeds

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Healing needs protein for the new tissue, calories for energy, vitamin C for collagen and zinc for cell division, all with adequate fluid

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — containing only liquids: A liquid diet alone rarely supplies enough protein and calories

B — restricted in fluids to keep the ulcer dry: Restricting fluids causes dehydration and poor tissue perfusion

question: The body mass index is calculated as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in metres

B — weight in kilograms multiplied by height in metres: Multiplying the two gives a meaningless value

question: A 35-year-old woman has a haemoglobin of 7 grams per decilitre and heavy bleeding during her periods. The nurse should advise her to:

question: Which practice causes the greatest loss of vitamin C from vegetables?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. prolonged cooking in a large quantity of water in an open vessel and then draining the water

question: The correct way to lift a heavy patient is to:

question: A 68-year-old man who had a stroke suddenly coughs and becomes breathless while being fed. The nurse should:

question: A 55-year-old patient receiving potassium chloride through a peripheral line complains of pain and burning along the vein with redness around it. The nurse should:

question: The earliest sign of a pressure ulcer is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a red area over a bony prominence that does not turn white when pressed

question: A 35-year-old man has sudden severe pain in the right lower abdomen with vomiting and a temperature of 38.2 degrees Celsius. The nurse should:

question: A woman at 32 weeks of pregnancy has painless vaginal bleeding with a soft, non tender uterus and the fetus is in an oblique lie. The nurse should:
solution:

question: A 4-year-old child has a harsh barking cough with a hoarse voice and noisy breathing that is worse at night. The child is alert with no drooling. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. keep the child calm and upright, avoid examining the throat, humidify the air and arrange medical review and observation for signs of airway obstruction

question: The preferred site for an intramuscular injection in an infant is the:

question: A 10-month-old infant has a fever, a bulging fontanelle, is refusing feeds and has had two episodes of vomiting. The nurse should:

question: The drug given to reduce fever in a child who is at risk of febrile convulsions is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. paracetamol in the prescribed dose

question: A patient taking antitubercular treatment complains of tingling and numbness in both feet. The likely cause is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. isoniazid, and pyridoxine is given with it to prevent this

question: The normal resting respiratory rate of a healthy adult is:
solution:

question: A patient who was trapped for several hours under rubble after a building collapse has dark brown urine with a urine output of 15 millilitres an hour. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. report the finding at once and give the prescribed fluids, since the dark urine and low output suggest muscle damage with impending kidney failure

💎 PNC Pearl: The urine output is measured hourly, and a fall below half a millilitre per kilogram per hour is reported immediately

question: A 45-year-old man with severe depression says that there is no point in living any longer. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. ask him directly about thoughts of suicide and any plan, do not leave him alone, and inform the treating team so that safety can be ensured

question: Which set of findings suggests neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a patient taking an antipsychotic drug?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. high fever with severe muscular rigidity, altered consciousness and unstable blood pressure and pulse

question: Whooping cough is caused by:

question: The spread of cancer cells through the blood stream to distant organs is called:
solution:

question: In a mass casualty situation the most important administrative task of the nursing officer is to:
solution:

question: The normal blood urea level in a healthy adult is about:

question: The largest organ of the human body is:

question: The most abundant gas in the atmosphere of the earth is:

question: The normal daily urine output of a healthy adult is about:

question: A solution of 0.9 percent sodium chloride is described as:

question: The drug given immediately in organophosphate insecticide poisoning is:

question: A closed room is fumigated with formaldehyde by mixing it with:

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1.5 degrees: One point five would give a temperature of thirty eight point five

B — 2 degrees: Two degrees would give thirty nine degrees exactly

C — 3.5 degrees: Three point five would give forty point five

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The rise above normal is what is reported to the doctor, since the same reading means different things in a child and in an elderly patient

question: If 15 tablets cost 45 rupees, the cost of 20 tablets at the same rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 60 rupees

🧠 Method: One tablet costs three rupees, so twenty tablets cost sixty rupees

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 90 rupees: Ninety rupees is the cost of thirty tablets

B — 50 rupees: Fifty rupees would need a lower rate

C — 75 rupees: Seventy five rupees would be twenty five tablets

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working out the cost per tablet is a quick way to compare two brands of the same medicine when a family has to pay for it themselves

question: An ambulance covers 240 kilometres in 4 hours on the outward journey and returns over the same distance in 6 hours. Its average speed for the whole journey is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 48 kilometres per hour

🧠 Method: The total distance is four hundred and eighty kilometres and the total time is ten hours, so the average speed is forty eight kilometres per hour

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 60 kilometres per hour: Sixty is only the speed of the outward journey

B — 45 kilometres per hour: Forty five is the average of the speeds taken differently

C — 50 kilometres per hour: Fifty is the simple mean of sixty and forty, which is wrong for unequal times

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The average speed is always the total distance divided by the total time, whatever the speeds on each part of the journey

question: In a village of 6000 persons, 45 percent are males. How many more females than males are there?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 600

🧠 Method: Forty five percent of 6000 is 2700 males, so the females number 3300, and the difference is 600

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 900: Nine hundred would mean females form sixty percent

B — 300: Three hundred would mean that females exceed males by only five percent

D — 1200: Twelve hundred would leave only forty percent as females

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Knowing the number of women of reproductive age and of children is what allows the expected number of pregnancies and the vaccine requirement to be worked out

question: If 7 pens cost 35 rupees, the cost of 12 pens at the same rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 60 rupees

🧠 Method: One pen costs five rupees, so twelve pens cost sixty rupees

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 72 rupees: Seventy two rupees would be the cost of about fourteen and a half pens

B — 48 rupees: Forty eight rupees would need a rate of four rupees each

D — 84 rupees: Eighty four rupees would be the cost of fourteen pens

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Finding the rate for one article first is the quickest and safest way to answer any question of this type

question: In a row of children, Meena is fourth from the left and third from the right. How many children are there in the row?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 6

🧠 Method: Adding the two positions gives seven, and one is subtracted because Meena has been counted twice, so there are six children

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 7: Seven is the sum of the two positions, in which Meena is counted twice

C — 8: Eight would need greater positions on either side

D — 5: Five is less than the sum of the positions minus one

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working out a position by counting both ways prevents the common error of counting or missing one person

question: P is the mother of Q, and Q is the sister of R. How is P related to R?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. mother

🧠 Method: Since Q and R are brother and sister, they have the same parents, so P is the mother of R as well

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — aunt: An aunt would be the sister of P and not P herself

C — sister: A sister of R would belong to the same generation as R

D — grandmother: A grandmother is the mother of P, who is not referred to at all

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Drawing the family as a simple tree on paper prevents the confusion that arises when such relations are worked out in the head

question: Arrange the following in a logical order: seed, fruit, flower, plant.
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. seed, plant, flower, fruit

🧠 Method: A seed gives rise to a plant, the plant bears a flower and the flower becomes the fruit

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — plant, seed, flower, fruit: A seed must come before the plant that grows from it

C — fruit, seed, plant, flower: The fruit comes at the end and not at the beginning

D — flower, fruit, seed, plant: The flower comes before the fruit and not after the seed

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Trick: Putting steps in the right order is the essence of a nursing procedure, where a change of sequence can make it unsafe

question: All nurses are graduates. Some graduates are teachers. Which of the following conclusions follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. neither of the conclusions that some nurses are teachers and that all graduates are nurses follows

🧠 Method: The teachers may be graduates who are not nurses, so nothing can be said about nurses being teachers, and the second statement reverses the given one

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — both conclusions follow: Neither conclusion follows, so not both

B — only the conclusion that all graduates are nurses follows: Only some graduates are nurses and not all of them

D — only the conclusion that some nurses are teachers follows: The nurses need not fall among the graduates who are teachers

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Keeping to what is certainly true and not what merely seems likely is the habit that prevents a wrong clinical conclusion

question: A cube of side 3 centimetres is painted on all its faces and then cut into cubes of 1 centimetre side. The number of small cubes with exactly two faces painted is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 12

🧠 Method: The cubes with two faces painted lie along the edges but not at the corners, and a cube has twelve edges with one such cube on each edge

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 8: Eight is the number of corner cubes, which have three faces painted

C — 24: Twenty four would count each edge cube twice

D — 6: Six is the number of faces of the cube

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working out a problem from a simple pattern, rather than drawing the whole figure, is a useful skill when time is short

question: If 2 is written as 8, 3 as 27 and 4 as 64, then 5 is written as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 125

🧠 Method: Each number is written as its cube, and the cube of five is one hundred and twenty five

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 25: Twenty five is the square of five and not its cube

C — 625: Six hundred and twenty five is the fourth power of five

D — 100: One hundred is the square of ten

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Finding the rule behind a set of figures, rather than memorising the answers, is what makes such questions quick and reliable
